newsitem.title: UK: AMEC considers investment in France's Spie.
newsitem.headline: AMEC considers investment in France's Spie.

text.p: AMEC Plc, the UK building group, said on Friday it is in talks with France's Spie Batignolle about getting support for a possible offer for its electrical and construction businesses from the holding company Schneider S.A.
Talks are still at an early stage, said an AMEC statement, with a number of details still to be thrashed out. A deal would be subject to agreement with the holding group Schneider.
If certain conditions are met, AMEC will make a strategic investment in Spie in the form of a minority holding.

The cost of this will be met from AMEC's existing cash resources and the stake would be the first step towards AMEC's aim of building a more international presence and possibly taking a controlling stake in Spie, it said.
The initial stake would give AMEC access to Spie's international network of regional bases offering partnership opprtunities on a cost efficient basis.
It would also add new skills which would help the two companies to pitch in growing markets like rail and airports.

AMEC and Spie management see a possible flotation of the French operation in due course and AMEC said a controlling stake for it could lead to the creation of a major European contractor with 40 percent of sales in the UK, 30 percent in France and 30 percent elsewhere.
If AMEC decides to proceed with the initial investment it sees completion by the year end.
Peter Mason, AMEC group chief executive, said in a statement "I have been most impressed with Spie's management team and the progress they have made in revitalising Spie."
He saw the deal as earnings enhancing.
Spie has 28,000 employees and operates in 290 locations. In its 1995 results after restructuring it reported turnover of 17 billion francs and an operating profit of 34 million francs.
